rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about criminal records before making a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods, and must do an individualized assessment and give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.
rules.key_value: Look-back after conditional offer: 6 years (first-degree), 4 years (second/third-degree), 1 year (fourth-degree); certain serious convictions and lifetime sex-offender registration have no limit
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (second), $10,000 (two or more others); director may order cease and desist, application fee return, and up to $1,000 paid to the applicant
rules.status_basis: Takes effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment (approved June 18, 2021).

exempt_if.text: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

coverage.summary: Applies to rental dwelling units offered for rent by housing providers.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.

rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
